project: Titanic source-first Belfast engineering photograph director cut
source_first_selection: 18 explicitly chosen source-matched historical visuals; exact narration 9x2 unchanged; no automated picture selection

shots.onscreen_label: BELFAST: TITANIC AND OLYMPIC UNDER CONSTRUCTION
shots.editorial_why: Actual historic shipyard construction establishing Harland & Wolff, Belfast.
Different real Titanic deck-construction photograph showing engineering scale, not a ship-at-sea image.

shots.onscreen_label: TITANIC AT THOMPSON DRY DOCK — FEBRUARY 1912
shots.editorial_why: Genuine dated dry-dock image grounds discussion of the ship's engineered hull; does not demonstrate watertight guarantees.

shots.onscreen_label: BULKHEADS: A DESIGNED LIMIT, NOT A GUARANTEE
shots.editorial_why: A labeled technical cross-section is required to reveal internal watertight divisions not accessible in period exterior photographs.
No April 1912 underwater film exists; schematic transparently explains inlet water.

shots.onscreen_label: WATER CAN SPILL OVER TOPS OF DIVISIONS — SCHEMATIC
shots.editorial_why: Historical evidence supports overtopping model; only a diagram can communicate spatial mechanism accurately.
Technical diagram needed to distinguish safe design envelopes from universal survival promises.
Contemporary Robert Welch photograph of Titanic's hull-launch engineering as an example of ambitious mechanical work, not evidence of watertight safety.

shots.onscreen_label: NOT A DOCUMENTED CONTINUOUS LONG GASH
shots.editorial_why: Directly refutes unsupported film depictions; no original photograph captures the exact 1912 iceberg damage.
Visibly labelled reconstructed explanatory geometry; no genuine photographic damage survey of the ship exists before sinking.
Historical archive dining room directly illustrates luxury accommodation; room/source caption requires final identity inspection.
A genuine first-class menu provides primary evidence of luxury service aboard, rather than artificial interiors.
Contemporary image of an actual Titanic shipbuilder questioned by the inquiry, directly pertinent to designers and inspected construction.

shots.onscreen_label: INSTALLING TITANIC'S STARBOARD TAIL SHAFT — MAY 1911
shots.editorial_why: Original Harland & Wolff technical work photograph shows documented actual machinery and proves scope of construction; not an inquiry photograph.

shots.onscreen_label: ACTUAL TITANIC STERN AND RUDDER IN DRY DOCK
shots.editorial_why: Period original image highlights exact stern and rudder mentioned by narrator, not imaginary mechanism.

shots.onscreen_label: GENUINE TITANIC BOW ON SLIPWAY — OCTOBER 1910
shots.editorial_why: Real dated bow construction photo complements the stern image without falsely reconstructing sinking.

shots.onscreen_label: TITANIC AT SOUTHAMPTON — BEFORE MAIDEN VOYAGE
shots.editorial_why: Actual ship photograph bridges shipyard topic to passengers with the correct port/time context.
Different genuine pre-disaster vessel photo illustrates imminent passenger voyage, not the final night.
